written: 2026-09-28, after the cell-side energy check reported that PyBaMM's heat source omits a heat of mixing of 83-128 % of the counted heat, and before any run of this test
hypothesis: Hc: the low heat-transfer coefficient calibrated in big14-a-lgm50-validation (3.555 W/m2K) partly compensates for heat the model omits (the heat of mixing). Stated as a post-hoc hypothesis from two earlier results; this is its first registered test.
setup: identical to big14-a-lgm50-validation (same pinned data, Chen2020 as shipped, SPM primary, lumped thermal, same calibration curve cell02 at 1C, same held-out set) except the PyBaMM option 'heat of mixing': 'true'

predictions.P1: the recalibrated heat-transfer coefficient is at least 20 % larger than 3.555 W/m2K
predictions.P2: over every held-out SPM temperature curve (all except cell02 at 1C), the mean |peak-rise error| is not larger than in big14-a-lgm50-validation (read from docs/flagships/big14/lgm50_validation_study.json)

not_claimed: neither outcome validates the thermal model; the reversible (entropic) heat stays absent because Chen2020 carries no entropic data
no_change_after_seeing_results: setup, predictions and thresholds are fixed
